title: Card transactions with fraud flags, September

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in night-time transactions
findings.detail: Night (0–5) transactions have a fraud rate of 30.8% against 0.3% to 0.7% in other periods. They are only 7% of rows (718), but 0.308 × 718 gives about 221 of the 272 fraud cases.

findings.headline: Digital goods and online channel carry the fraud
findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% fraud rate against 0.3% to 0.7% for other categories. Online is 6.3% against 0.3% for Contactless and 0.5% for Chip. These patterns go together and may overlap.

findings.headline: Fraud rate is very high in AE and SG
findings.detail: AE is at 28.6% (206 rows) and SG at 31% (187 rows), against 1.6% for IN. Together they are only 3.8% of rows, so a small share of volume drives a large share of risk.

findings.headline: Fraud rate rose sharply in mid-September
findings.detail: Weekly fraud rate went from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 1.7%, then 4.0% and 4.1% in the following two weeks. The last week is partial (727 rows), so its 1.8% is less reliable.

findings.headline: Smallest transactions have the highest fraud rate
findings.detail: The lowest amount band (1.71 to 535.9) has an 11.4% fraud rate. Every higher band is between 0.3% and 0.6%. Small test-style payments may be worth checking.

next_steps: Check how far night-time, online, digital goods, AE and SG overlap, to see whether one pattern explains most of the 272 fraud cases.
Review recent card IDs with small online digital-goods payments at night or abroad, and test tighter rules or step-up checks.
Find out what changed in the weeks of 14 and 21 September, and confirm whether the fraud labels are complete for the latest days.

conclusion: Fraud in this file is highly concentrated: night-time, digital goods, online, AE and SG, and small amounts all go with fraud rates far above the 2.7% overall. These groups probably overlap heavily, so treat them as one risk picture rather than five separate problems. First, work out how much they overlap, so any new rule targets the right combination.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show overlap between groups, why fraud is higher in them, or whether the fraud labels are complete.
